examples.en: It has been drizzling since morning, so the road is damp.

examples.ko: 이 정도 가랑비는 우산 없이 맞아도 괜찮아요.
examples.en: This much drizzle is fine to walk in without an umbrella.

examples.ko: 가랑비 오는 날에는 파전이 먹고 싶어요.
examples.en: On drizzly days I want to eat scallion pancakes.

examples.ko: 산책하는 동안 가랑비를 맞았더니 머리가 젖었어요.
examples.en: I got caught in the drizzle during my walk and my hair got wet.
I worried the sports day would be postponed because of the drizzle.
Outside the window, a fine rain like a drizzle is falling.

explain: 가늘게 조용히 내리는 비를 말해요. 이슬비, 보슬비도 비슷하게 가늘게 내리는 비이고, 반대 느낌은 갑자기 세게 쏟아지는 '소나기'예요. 속담에 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 작은 지출도 쌓이면 커져요. 가랑비에 옷 젖는 줄 모른다더니 카드값이 많이 나왔어요.
phrases.en: Small expenses pile up. As the saying goes, you don't notice a drizzle soaking your clothes, and my card bill came out high.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작고 사소한 것이라도 쌓이면 큰 영향을 준다는 속담이에요. 돈, 습관, 나쁜 버릇 이야기에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A proverb meaning that even small things have a big effect when they accumulate. Often used for money, habits and bad habits.
phrases.en_equiv: Many a little makes a mickle

explain_en: It is a thin, quiet rain. '이슬비' and '보슬비' are also fine, light rains, while the opposite feel is '소나기', a sudden heavy shower. It appears in a well-known proverb.

examples.en: Buds have started to form on the cherry tree.

examples.ko: 며칠 지나면 꽃봉오리가 활짝 필 거예요.
examples.en: In a few days the buds will bloom fully.
It's still a bud, so it's fine to put it in a vase.
I carefully touched the rose bud.

examples.ko: 봄비가 내린 뒤 꽃봉오리가 통통하게 부풀었어요.
examples.en: After the spring rain, the buds swelled up plump.
One flower bud burst open this morning.

explain: 활짝 핀 꽃은 '만개한 꽃', 아직 닫힌 상태는 '꽃봉오리'라고 구별해요. '봉오리'로 줄여 말하기도 하고, 앞날이 기대되는 어린 사람을 '꽃봉오리'에 비유하기도 해요.

phrases.en: A rosebud has come up in the flower bed.
phrases.nuance_ko: '꽃봉오리'를 줄인 말로, 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shortened form of '꽃봉오리' that is common in speech.

phrases.en: The weather was warm, so the flower buds opened.
phrases.nuance_ko: 닫혀 있던 꽃봉오리가 피기 시작할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for when a closed bud starts to open.

phrases.en: When spring came, flower buds formed on the branches.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꽃봉오리가 처음 생길 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for when buds first form.

explain_en: A fully open flower is 만개한 꽃, while one still closed is a 꽃봉오리. It is also shortened to '봉오리', and a promising young person is sometimes compared to a 꽃봉오리.

examples.en: At night, moths gathered near the light.
A moth came in through the window.

examples.ko: 나방은 나비보다 색이 어두운 경우가 많아요.
examples.en: Moths are often darker in color than butterflies.
I was startled when a moth came out of the closet.
The moth caterpillars ate all the leaves.
I'm scared of moths, so I avoid them.

explain: 나비는 낮에 날고 앉을 때 날개를 접는 경우가 많고, 나방은 밤에 날고 앉을 때 날개를 펴는 경우가 많아요. 밤에 불빛에 모이는 모습 때문에 '불나방'이라는 말도 있는데, 위험한 줄 모르고 뛰어드는 사람을 비유할 때 써요.

phrases.en: Don't jump into dangerous things like a moth to a flame.
phrases.nuance_ko: 불빛에 모이는 나방에서 나온 말로, 위험한 줄 모르는 사람을 비유해요.
phrases.nuance_en: From moths drawn to light; compares someone who rushes into danger without knowing it.

phrases.en: Many moths fly around on summer nights.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나방이 날아다니는 모습을 말할 때 쓰는 문장이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A sentence for describing moths flying around.

phrases.en: Butterflies and moths look alike.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두 곤충을 비교하거나 함께 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when comparing the two insects or mentioning them together.

explain_en: Butterflies tend to fly by day and fold their wings when they rest, while moths tend to fly at night and keep their wings spread when they rest. Because moths gather around lights at night, there is also the word '불나방', used figuratively for someone who rushes into danger without realizing it.

en: to be gently warm; to be softly warm (sunlight)

examples.en: The spring sunshine is warm, so I feel sleepy.
Grandmother's hands were always warm.

examples.ko: 따스한 차 한 잔을 마시니까 마음이 편해졌어요.
examples.en: Drinking a cup of warm tea made me feel at ease.

examples.ko: 그 사람의 따스한 말 한마디에 힘이 났어요.
examples.en: A single warm word from him gave me strength.
When the weather gets warm, let's go on a picnic together.

examples.ko: 따스하게 안아 주는 친구 덕분에 위로가 됐어요.
examples.en: A friend who hugged me warmly comforted me.

explain: '따뜻하다'와 거의 같지만 따스하다는 더 부드럽고 글이나 노래에서 자주 나와요. 햇살, 손, 말, 마음처럼 포근한 것에 잘 어울려요. 뜨거운 국이나 방바닥에는 '따뜻하다'나 '뜨겁다'를 쓰는 편이 자연스러워요.

phrases.example: 따스한 말 한마디가 큰 힘이 돼요.
phrases.en: A warm word can be a great help.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람의 말이나 마음이 포근할 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone's words or heart feel gentle and comforting.

phrases.example: 할머니가 따스하게 웃으며 저를 안아 주셨어요.
phrases.en: My grandmother hugged me with a warm smile.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-게'를 붙이면 웃는 모습이나 대하는 방식을 부드럽게 꾸며 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -게 describes how someone smiles or treats others, in a soft way.

phrases.en: The winter wind is not warm.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 포근하지 않다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, saying something is not gently warm.

explain_en: It is nearly the same as 따뜻하다, but 따스하다 is softer and appears more in writing and songs. It suits cozy things like sunlight, hands, words, and hearts. For hot soup or a heated floor, 따뜻하다 or 뜨겁다 sounds more natural.

examples.en: White fluffy clouds are floating in the sky.
Fluffy clouds remind me of cotton candy.
The shape of puffy clouds keeps changing.
Sunlight shone through the puffy clouds.
It's a cake as fluffy as a cloud.
I want to lie down on the fluffy clouds.

explain: 몽실몽실하게 위로 솟은 하얀 구름이에요. 맑은 날 여름 하늘에서 많이 보여서 그림이나 동요, 시에 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: The white puffy clouds in the blue sky are pretty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 구름 색을 앞에 붙여서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used with a color word before it.

phrases.en: Puffy clouds rose up in the summer sky.
phrases.nuance_ko: 구름이 위로 솟아오르는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes clouds billowing upward.

phrases.en: Puffy clouds are floating above the mountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 구름이 하늘에 있는 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the state of clouds being in the sky.

explain_en: These are white clouds that billow upward in rounded puffs. They are often seen in clear summer skies and appear in drawings, children's songs and poems.

examples.en: I keep a small cactus on my desk.

examples.ko: 선인장은 물을 자주 안 줘도 돼요.
examples.en: A cactus doesn't need to be watered often.
I pricked my finger on a cactus spine.
Big cacti grow in great numbers in the desert.
A yellow flower bloomed on the cactus!

examples.ko: 바쁜 사람에게는 선인장 같은 식물을 추천해요.
examples.en: For busy people, I recommend plants like a cactus.

explain: '선인장'은 줄기에 물을 저장해서 물을 적게 줘도 사는 식물이에요. 잎이나 줄기에 물을 저장하는 식물 전체는 '다육식물'이라고 하고, 선인장은 그중 한 종류예요. '가시'와 함께 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: I got pricked by a cactus thorn.
phrases.nuance_ko: 선인장과 가장 자주 같이 말하는 부분이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The part most often mentioned together with cactus.

phrases.en: I grow a cactus on my balcony.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식물을 기를 때는 '키우다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 키우다 for growing a plant.

phrases.example: 선인장에는 한 달에 한 번 물을 줘요.
phrases.en: I water the cactus once a month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식물에 물을 줄 때는 '에 물을 주다'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: To water a plant, say 에 물을 주다.

explain_en: A 선인장 is a plant that stores water in its stem and survives on very little. The broader group of plants that store water in leaves or stems is 다육식물, and 선인장 is one kind of them. It is often mentioned together with 가시 (thorns).

examples.en: On a clear day, I suddenly got caught in a sun shower.

examples.ko: 여우비는 금방 그치니까 우산 없이 기다려 봐요.
examples.en: A sun shower stops soon, so let's wait without an umbrella.
After the sun shower, a rainbow appeared in the sky.
The sun was bright and yet a sun shower fell, which was amazing.

examples.ko: 여우비 때문에 잠깐 처마 밑에 서 있었어요.
examples.en: Because of the sun shower, I stood under the eaves for a moment.
It was just a sun shower today, so I ran without an umbrella.

explain: 해가 떠 있는데 잠깐 내리다 그치는 비예요. 오래 쏟아지는 '소나기'와 달리 날이 맑은 채로 금방 지나가는 비를 말해요. 날씨 이야기에서 가볍게 쓰는 순우리말이에요.

phrases.en: A sun shower fell suddenly in the afternoon.
phrases.nuance_ko: '비가 내리다'처럼 여우비가 오는 것을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Like 비가 내리다, it says that a sun shower is falling.

phrases.en: I got caught in a sun shower while taking a walk.
phrases.nuance_ko: 밖에 있다가 갑자기 비를 맞았을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you are outside and run into the rain unexpectedly.
phrases.en_equiv: to get caught in a sun shower

phrases.example: 여우비가 금방 그쳐서 다시 해가 났어요.
phrases.en: The sun shower stopped soon and the sun came out again.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잠깐 오고 그치는 여우비의 특징을 보여 주는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shows the short-lived nature of a sun shower.

explain_en: It is rain that falls briefly while the sun is out. Unlike a '소나기' (shower) that pours hard, this is rain that passes quickly while the sky stays clear. It is a native Korean word used lightly in weather talk.

examples.en: It's a summer afternoon with the sun blazing down.

examples.ko: 쨍쨍 비치는 햇볕 때문에 눈이 부셔요.
examples.en: The glaring sunshine is dazzling my eyes.

examples.ko: 어제는 해가 쨍쨍 나서 빨래가 잘 말랐어요.
examples.en: Yesterday the sun was shining brightly, so the laundry dried well.

examples.ko: 해가 쨍쨍 뜬 날에는 모자를 꼭 써요.
examples.en: On days when the sun is blazing, I always wear a hat.

examples.ko: 쨍쨍 더운 날 밖에서 일하면 힘들어요.
examples.en: Working outside on a blazing hot day is hard.

examples.ko: 햇볕이 쨍쨍 나자 아이들이 물놀이를 시작했어요.
examples.en: When the sun came out brightly, the children started playing in the water.

explain: 햇볕이 아주 밝고 강하게 비치는 모양이에요. '해가 쨍쨍 나다', '햇볕이 쨍쨍 내리쬐다'처럼 날씨 이야기에서 주로 쓰고, 구름이 없는 맑은 날의 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.example: 오늘은 해가 쨍쨍 나서 빨래가 잘 말라요.
phrases.en: The sun is blazing today, so the laundry dries well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 구름 없이 맑고 햇볕이 강한 날씨를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for clear weather with strong sunshine and no clouds.

phrases.en: The sunshine is bright and strong today.
phrases.nuance_ko: '쨍쨍'에 '-하다'를 붙여 날씨를 설명하는 형용사로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-하다' to '쨍쨍' makes an adjective for describing the weather.

phrases.en: We went on a picnic on a bright, sunny day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 명사를 붙여서 맑고 햇볕이 센 날씨를 설명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put before a noun to describe clear, sunny weather.

explain_en: It describes sunlight shining very bright and strong. It mostly appears in weather talk, as in '해가 쨍쨍 나다' or '햇볕이 쨍쨍 내리쬐다', and gives the feeling of a clear, cloudless day.

examples.ko: 봄이 되면 산에 분홍 철쭉이 가득 피어요.
examples.en: When spring comes, pink royal azaleas bloom all over the mountain.

examples.ko: 주말에 철쭉 축제를 보러 가족과 함께 갔어요.
examples.en: On the weekend I went to the azalea festival with my family.

examples.ko: 길가에 핀 철쭉이 거리를 예쁘게 꾸몄어요.
examples.en: Azaleas along the road decorated the street beautifully.
Royal azaleas bloom a little later than Korean azaleas.
I saw people planting azaleas in the park.
My mother took photos of the azaleas with her phone.

explain: 철쭉은 진달래와 비슷하지만 조금 더 늦게, 잎과 함께 피는 경우가 많아요. 진달래꽃은 먹을 수 있어도 철쭉은 독이 있어서 먹으면 안 돼요. 봄 산 이야기에서 둘이 같이 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: Royal azalea flowers have bloomed prettily along the mountain path.
phrases.nuance_ko: '꽃'을 붙여 꽃 자체를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 꽃 to refer to the flower itself.

phrases.en: Many royal azaleas bloom in May.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꽃이 열릴 때는 '피다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 피다 when flowers bloom.

phrases.en: I went to see the azaleas with my family on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꽃을 보러 가는 일은 '구경'을 붙여 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 구경 for going to see flowers.

explain_en: 철쭉 looks like 진달래 but blooms a bit later, often together with its leaves. 진달래 flowers can be eaten, but 철쭉 is poisonous and must not be. The two often come up together in talk about spring mountains.

examples.en: A white crane is standing by the lake.

examples.ko: 학은 오래 사는 동물로 알려져 있어요.
examples.en: The crane is known as a long-living animal.
I saw a crane for the first time at the zoo.

examples.ko: 그림 속에 학 두 마리가 날고 있어요.
examples.en: Two cranes are flying in the painting.

examples.ko: 한국 옛 그림에는 소나무와 학이 자주 나와요.
examples.en: Pine trees and cranes often appear in old Korean paintings.

examples.ko: 학처럼 다리가 긴 새는 물가에서 살아요.
examples.en: Birds with long legs like cranes live near the water.

explain: 한국 옛 그림에서 학은 오래 사는 동물이라 건강과 오래 사는 삶을 빌 때 소나무와 함께 그려요. 같은 새를 순우리말로는 '두루미'라고 하는데, 일상에서는 '학'과 '두루미'를 둘 다 써요. '학교'의 '학'과는 소리만 같고 전혀 다른 말이에요.

phrases.example: 겨울에 두루미가 눈 위에 앉아 있어요.
phrases.en: In winter, cranes sit on the snow.
phrases.nuance_ko: '학'과 같은 새를 가리키는 순우리말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A native Korean word for the same bird as '학'.

phrases.en: The crane flies slowly across the sky.
phrases.nuance_ko: '학'에 '날다'를 붙여 새가 나는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairing '학' with '날다' describes the bird flying.

phrases.example: 친구를 위해 종이학을 천 마리 접었어요.
phrases.en: I folded a thousand paper cranes for my friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 종이로 접은 학을 가리키고, 소원을 빌 때 많이 접어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a crane folded from paper, often made as a wish.

explain_en: In old Korean paintings the crane stands for a long, healthy life, so it is often drawn with pine trees. The native Korean word for the same bird is '두루미', and both words are used. It sounds the same as the '학' in '학교' (school), but they are unrelated.

en: to burn; to glow; to flush

examples.en: It's stifling hot inside the bus in midsummer.
I lit the stove and the room got toasty hot.

examples.ko: 얼굴이 후끈한 걸 보니 열이 있는 것 같아요.
examples.en: My face feels hot, so I think I have a fever.

examples.ko: 후끈하게 데운 국물을 마시니 몸이 풀려요.
examples.en: Drinking the piping hot broth relaxes my body.

examples.ko: 경기장 분위기가 후끈해서 모두 소리를 질렀어요.
examples.en: The stadium atmosphere was fired up, so everyone cheered loudly.

examples.ko: 오븐 문을 열자 후끈한 바람이 나왔어요.
examples.en: When I opened the oven door, a blast of hot air came out.

explain: 공기나 몸이 덥고 열이 확 오르는 느낌에 써요. '따뜻하다'보다 열기가 세고 '뜨겁다'보다는 부드러워요. 사람의 열정이나 분위기가 뜨거울 때도 '분위기가 후끈하다'라고 써요.

phrases.en: When I opened the door, hot, stuffy air came out.
phrases.nuance_ko: '후끈하다'를 꾸미는 말(~ㄴ)로 바꿔 명사 앞에 붙여 쓸 때예요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the modifier form, used right before a noun.

phrases.en: I'm embarrassed, so my face feels hot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸이나 얼굴에 열이 확 오를 때 써요. 날씨뿐 아니라 감정에도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when heat rushes to your body or face, from weather or from emotion.

phrases.en: When the song started, the mood heated up.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어지다'를 붙이면 열기나 분위기가 점점 뜨거워지는 변화를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -아/어지다 shows the heat or mood growing stronger.

explain_en: It describes air or a body that feels hot with heat rising suddenly. It is stronger than '따뜻하다' but gentler than '뜨겁다'. A passionate mood can also be '분위기가 후끈하다'.
